query: Screen sharing stopped working after upgrading to Electron 45 even though my setPermissionRequestHandler allows 'media'. Why?
goldAnswer: Electron 45 reports screen, window and tab capture requests to `setPermissionRequestHandler` as `display-capture` instead of `media`, so the handler must also allow `display-capture`.

query: Why does python -m ruff no longer work after updating Ruff to 0.17 from conda-forge?
goldAnswer: Ruff 0.17.0's conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, so `python -m ruff` and `import ruff` fail; run `ruff` from PATH instead.

query: Tailwind CSS v4 CLI --watch doesn't detect changes when filesystem events are unavailable. How do I fix it?
goldAnswer: Run `@tailwindcss/cli` with `--watch --poll` (optionally `--poll=<ms>`); polling support was added in Tailwind CSS v4.3.3.

query: In September 2026, ESA hailed what it called the first launch to orbit from continental Europe. In which town was the company that built that rocket headquartered?

query: My PostgREST jwt-role-claim-key of ".roles.read" stopped working after upgrading to v16.0. What's the new syntax?
goldAnswer: Prefix it with `$`, e.g. `$.roles.read` (PostgREST v16.0 switched `jwt-role-claim-key` from its JSPath DSL to RFC 9535 JSON Path; v16.2 accepts the old syntax again but deprecates it).

query: In October 2026 the CGPM fixed the date in 2027 from which UTC will be continuous, with no more leap seconds. Which annual UNESCO international day falls on that date?
goldAnswer: World Metrology Day (continuous UTC starts on 20 May 2027; 20 May marks the 1875 signing of the Metre Convention).

query: In its 'Trojan' rulings published in August 2025, Germany's Federal Constitutional Court held that using state trojan spyware (source telecommunications surveillance) in criminal investigations is unconstitutional for offences carrying a maximum prison sentence of how many years or less?
goldAnswer: 3 years [the court declared source telecommunications surveillance under the Code of Criminal Procedure void for offences carrying a maximum sentence of three years or less; orders of 24 June 2025, published 7 August 2025]

query: Under Portugal's legal safe harbour for good-faith security researchers (Article 8-A of the Cybercrime Law, added by a decree-law published in December 2025), within how many days of a reported vulnerability being fixed must the data handed to the system owner or the national cybersecurity authority be deleted?
goldAnswer: 10 days [counted from when the vulnerability is corrected; Article 8.º-A(4) of Lei n.º 109/2009, added by Decreto-Lei n.º 125/2025]

query: In Vue 3.6, a `<style scoped>` rule whose selector list mixes a plain selector with a `:deep()` one and contains a nested rule, e.g. `.a, .b :deep(.c) { color: red; > span { color: blue; } }`, compiles with `.a` missing the `[data-v-xxx]` attribute, so it leaks globally. Why, and how do I work around it?
goldAnswer: A compiler-sfc scoped-CSS bug: when the rule has nested child rules, the `:deep()` in one selector-list member changes how the other members get scoped. Work around it by not mixing `:deep()` and plain scoped selectors in the same selector list: split them into separate rules (`.a { ... }` and `.b :deep(.c) { ... }`) [maintainer-confirmed workaround; reported on 3.6.0-rc.2, issue still open on 12 Nov 2026]

query: After updating my NixOS system to the latest nixos-unstable, Slint apps built from my project flake (which pins an older nixpkgs) still run but never open a window with the default femtovg renderer, and print no error; the Skia renderer works. What's the cause and how do I fix it?
goldAnswer: A glibc mismatch: the app is built against its flake's older nixpkgs glibc, but the system's newer Mesa graphics drivers that Slint loads expect the system's glibc, so the default femtovg renderer fails silently; include the graphics stack in the app's flake, run the app through a wrapper such as nixGL, or update the flake's nixpkgs to match the system [Slint gets no error back from EGL, so it has nothing to report]

query: After upgrading from TypeScript 6.0 to 7.0, a JS file where an arrow function has a JSDoc block with `@template T` and `@type {(v: T) => T}` now errors with TS2304: Cannot find name 'T'. It compiled under TS 6. Why does TS 7 reject it, and how should the `@type` tag be written instead?
goldAnswer: Not a regression: `@template` isn't supposed to apply to a `@type` tag (TS 6 accepting it was a bug), so declare the type parameter inside the type itself: `/** @type {<T>(v: T) => T} */` [in TS 6 the combination leaked an unbound `T`, e.g. `id(42)` was typed as `T`; the issue was closed as Working as Intended]

query: error: Type of "queue" could not be determined because it refers to itself (reportGeneralTypeIssues)
goldAnswer: A name clash: the attribute is named `queue`, like the `queue` module used in its own annotation (`queue: queue.Queue` after `import queue`), so Pyright resolves `queue` in the annotation to the attribute itself; avoid the clash, e.g. rename the attribute (`q: queue.Queue`), or target Python 3.14+ [it happens under Python 3.13-and-earlier annotation semantics, while with 3.14's deferred annotations (PEP 649/749) Pyright resolves the name differently; it reproduces on old Pyright versions such as 1.1.364, so it isn't a regression; the maintainer calls it expected on 3.13 and earlier but says it may always have been a Pyright bug; importing the class directly (`from queue import Queue`) also avoids the clash]
